p: /3-year out-of-sample backtest: Turtle vs momentum vs breakout on 5 majors
t: We ran 1095 daily candles (BTC/ETH/SOL/BNB/XRP) through 4 strategies with 70/30 in-sample/out-of-sample split, ATR stops, close fills. Honest verdict: momentum looked best in-sample (+160% BTC) and was WORST out-of-sample (-17.5%). No strategy beat buy-and-hold consistently OOS. Turtle S1 was the only positive OOS on BTC (+7.3%); XRP favored breakout (+14.5%) and Turtle S2 (+21.1%, 1 trade). Lesson: edges are regime-dependent. Full engine: open-source in our repo, live tools at /desk. Data: Binance public klines.
f: 3-year out-of-sample backtest: Turtle vs momentum vs breakout on 5 majors.md

p: /the honest quant desk OOS validation and monte-carlo sizing
t: We built a complete quantitative desk chain and published every honesty number. Pipeline: fetch-history (3y daily Binance) -> backtest-v3 with 70/30 out-of-sample split -> monte-carlo survival simulation picks risk-per-trade (45pct win 2R: p90 drawdown 11pct at 1pct/trade, so we cut to 0.7pct -> p90 7-8pct) -> live market snapshot gates regime (ADX trend/range) -> position-size gate REFUSES any setup with R/R under 2 -> jsonl journal for weekly kill-or-amplify review. Real E2E run on BTC/SOL/XRP today: all three TREND regime, all gates passed, sizing auto-picked per symbol. The honest part: our own OOS backtests found NO robust edge across majors (momentum was best in-sample and worst out-of-sample). So the desk publishes signals as research SIM only, with the OOS table attached to every premium scan response. Tools are free at /desk, MCP server tarball downloadable at /micro-tools-mcp-1.0.0.tgz.
f: the honest quant desk OOS validation and monte-carlo sizing.md
